This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.1,50,00,000/- for the death of Shivaswamy.T.E S/o Late Eshwaraiah in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 02.01.2023 at about 10.30 a.m., the deceased Shivaswamy was travelling back home from his office work on his motor cycle bearing reg No.KA-42-R-0791 from Channapattana to Bangalore, when he reached Channapatna Police Training School on Mysore-Bangalore road, at that time driver of the bus bearing No.KA-42-A-9990 (Udayaranga bus) driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the heavy impact, the Shivaswamy T.E fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
The Postmortem was conducted at Channapatna Government Hospital, Channapatna and dead body was handed over to the Petitioners.

Prior to the accident, said Shivaswamy T.E was hale and healthy and he was working as Technical Operator Drilling in the Central Ground Water Board and was earning a sum of Rs.79,978/- per month and he got one more promotion for Super-annuation.
The deceased family entirely depending on the income of the deceased.
The petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and towards funeral obsequies.
The said accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-A-9990.

The Respondent No.1 is the Sunitha.S vs Kavitha R.N on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143693310/
2 owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-A-9990.
Therefore, both the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
3. Despite service of notice, Respondent No.1 remained absent, hence she was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed its objection.

Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement to the main petition denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus.

Further it disputes issuance of policy of insurance in favour of the 1 st Respondent in respect of Udayaranga bus bearing Reg. No.KA-42-A-9990, the liability of this respondent company if any is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy and subject to valid and effective driving licence of the rider in question and subject to confirmation of 64VB of Insurance Act, 1938.

Further it denies the occurrence of the alleged accident involving the Udayaranga Bus bearing Reg No.KA-42-A-9990, the Petitioner hand in glove with the police authorities falsely foisted/implicated the insured vehicle, in order to make unlawful monetary gain.
Further contended that the accident occurred on account negligence on part the deceased who was riding Motorcycle in rash and negligent manner and lost control and fell down.

On these grounds,
Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival pleadings, the following Issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that Shri.Shivaswamy.T.E S/o Eshwaraiah was died in the Road Traffic Accident which occurred on 02-01-2023 at about 10.30 a.m., on Mysore-Bangalore road, near Channapatna Police Training school, Ramanagara, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of bus bearing No.KA-42-A-9990?
2. Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Shri.Shivaswamy.T.E?

3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for? If yes,
what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
4. What Order or Award?

5. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner No.2 got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 22 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 22 and examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 6 documents as per Ex.P.23 to Ex.P28 closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 has not chosen to lead evidence.

6. I have heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2, perused the depositions and documents Sunitha.S vs Kavitha R.N on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143693310/
3 exhibited and materials available on record.

7. My answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative. Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 8.

Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioner that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-A-9990 and in the said accident, Shivaswamy.T.E had succumbed to the injuries.
9. On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus.

10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, Petitioner No.2 got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 22 documents at Ex.P.1 to 22 and he has filed his chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and re-iterated the petition averments.
11.
PW.1 has relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.22.

Ex.P.1 is the True copy of FIR and Ex.P.2 is the complaint, they show that Channapatna Police have registered the case against the driver of bus bearing No.KA-42-A-9990 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Ex . P.3
and Ex
. P.9 the Spot Mahazar and Sketch show that IO has drawn the same in the presence of panchas.
The exact accident spot is marked in the sketch, which shows that the accident was taken place in the left side of the road.

In the said mahazar there is a recital that the when the deceased was proceeding on his bike on left side of the road the offending bus had came from same direction and dashed against him from behind.

Therefore, contention of Respondent No.2 that the accident occurred on account negligence on part the deceased who was riding Motorcycle in rash and negligent manner and lost control and fell down does not have any water.
Thereby no grounds are made out to consider the contributory negligence of the deceased.

Ex.P.6 is the certified copy of the Charge-sheet, which shows that the I.O had submitted Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending bus for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.7 is the Inquest report and Ex.P.8 is the PM report, which shows that death is due to shock and hemorrhage as a result of multiple skull bone fractures and injuries to vital organ brain.

Ex.P.10 is the IMV Report, which shows that accident did not occur due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle and the damages found on the both vehicles justify the involvement of vehicles in the accident.
Ex.P.11 is the notice under Sec.133 of IMV Act, which shows that the IO had called upon the owner of the offending vehicle to produce the DL of driver and documents of the vehicle.
Ex . P.12

4 Ex.P13 is the reply given to the said notice, which shows that the one C. Gangaraju had admitted that Sharath.K was the driver of the bus at the time of accident and he also furnished the details of DL of offending driver and insurance policy details.
Ex.P.14 is the voluntary statement of driver of offending bus which shows that he admitted the nature of accident.
Ex.P.15 is copies of photos.
Ex.P.16 is certified copy of certificate U/s 65 B of Evidence Act.

Ex.P.20 is the notarized copy of Aadhar card of petitioner No.1.
Ex.P.21 is notarized copy of ID card and Ex.P.22 is the notarized copy of DL of the Deceased.
12. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 has cross examined the P.W.1 in lengthy.
In the cross-examination, PW.1 admitted that he has not seen the occurrence of the accident.
Therefore, his evidence would not be deciding factor for the negligence.
13. Accident is not in dispute.
Only the fact of negligence is disputed by the respondent No.2.

Though the Respondent No.2 has taken contention that the accident did not cause due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, but it did not lead any evidence to substantiate its contentions.
The main contention of the Respondent No.2 is that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself.
But, it has not produced cogent evidence to prove its contention.
The Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending bus has not chosen to contest the case.

As discussed above, the mahazar and spot sketch clearly disclose that the driver of the offending bus had drove his bus in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased motor cycle from behind who proceeding on the left side of the road.

Hence,
the petitioners successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of the offending bus.
Moreover, after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending bus and the driver of the bus had not challenged the charge sheet.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus bearing No.KA-42-A-9990 and due to the said accident,
Shivaswamy
. T.E., succumbed to the injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in the "Affirmative".
14. Issue No.2

and 3 : Both these issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid the repetition of the facts.
15.
It is stated in the Petition that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner no.2 is the son and Petitioner no.3 is the mother of the deceased.
In order to prove this fact, PW 1 has produced Ex.P.17 i.e., Aadhar Card of the deceased Shivaswamy.T.E. and Ex.P.18 to 20 Aadhar cards of petitioners.
Upon going through the said Aadhar cards and contents of police papers do fortify the said fact.
Moreover there is no dispute about the relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
Hence, it is held that the petitioners have proved that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Shivaswamy.T.E.

Therefore, the Petitioners are considered as the dependents of the deceased Shivaswamy.T.E.

In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 52 years and his avocation is shown as Technical operator drilling in the Central ground water board and was earning a sum of Rs.79,978/-
per month.
17. To prove the age of deceased the petitioners have produced the Ex.P.17-Aadhar card.
As per Aadhar card of the deceased Shivaswamy.T.E the year of the birth of Shivaswamy.T.E was shown as 1971.
The accident was occurred on 02.01.2023.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Shivaswamy.T.E was 52 years.
Hence, the age of the deceased Shivaswamy.T.E to be taken at 52 years for the purpose of Assessment of compensation.
18. In order to prove the income of deceased the petitioners have produced Last pay certificate of deceased marked at Ex.P.5.
Which shows that his gross salary was Rs.79,872/- and deduction of a sum of Rs.5200/- towards income tax and Rs.200 towards professional tax.
In addition to this petitioners have examined Executive Manager of Central Ground Water Board as PW.2.
He deposed that the deceased Shivaswamy was working as Technical Operator, Drilling in their company since 6.7.1992 till his death i.e., on 02.01.2023.
He further deposed that the deceased was drawing salary of Rs.79,878/-.
In support of his version he has produced Ex.P23 and 24 - Salary Certificates,
Ex.P25 is the Biometric Attendance register extract, Ex.P26 is the Letter issued by the Central Ground Water Board, Ex.P27 is the authorization letter, Ex.P28 is the Service register of the deceased.
19. In the cross examination of PW.2, he admitted that, as per Ex.P23 and Ex.P24, Rs.5000/- was deducted towards income tax, Rs.200/- was deducted towards professional tax.
Further he admitted that Rs.4968/- is travel allowance.
20. Learned counsel for the Respondent No.2 vehemently argues that travel allowance should be deducted from the gross salary for considering the income of deceased.

21. At this juncture it is profitable to refer the reportable judgment of hon'ble Supreme Court in Meenakshi Vs The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd (Petition for Special Leave to Appeal (c)
No.39746/2018) decided on 23.07.2024.

entities.text:
Meenakshi Vs The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd (Petition for Special Leave to Appeal (c)
No.39746/2018)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein it is held that, allowance under the heads of transport allowance, house rent allowance, provident fund loan, provident fund and special allowance ought to be added while considering the basic salary of the victim/deceased to arrive at the dependency factor.
22. Keeping the aforesaid principles in mind considered the case on hand.
As per Ex.P.24-Salary slip, his gross income per month was Rs.79,878/- for the month of December, 2022 i.e., his last pay.
Wherein, Rs.5,000/- was deducted towards income tax and Rs.200/- was deducted towards professional tax.
Hence these amount does not come under the income.
Other deductions cannot be deducted as those deduction also come under the income.
After deducting the professional tax and income tax his income would be Rs.74,678/-.
Therefore, Rs.74,678/- p.m. is taken as income of petitioner for the purpose of assessment of compensation.

6 23.
With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I.
COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
24. The deceased has left behind him, his wife, a son and his mother.
Hence, the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are considered as dependents.

25. At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/ s Pranay Sethi and Others).

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/ s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/-, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/-".
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced @ 10% in every three years."
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife, the petitioner No.2 is the son and petitioner No.3 is the mother of the deceased.
Petitioner No.1 has to live remaining part of her life in the absence of her husband and the loss of a husband full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to a wife.
Petitioner No.2 has to live remaining part of his life in the absence of his father.
Petitioner No.3 has to live remaining part of her life in the absence of her son and the loss of a son full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to a son.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- each under the head of loss of consortium and Rupees 16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rupees 16,500/- towards funeral expenses.

II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
26.

Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's love and care, Petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased and they lost his father's love and care and Petitioner No.3 is the mother of the deceased have lost her son's love and care.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
27.
The dead body was shifted to Channapatna Government hospital for post mortem.
The petitioner are residing in Lakshman Nagar, Hegganahalli Cross, Bangalore.
Hence they might have buried the dead body nearby to their residence.
Hence, the Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.10,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

IV.COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:
28.

It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was Rs.74,678/- p.m.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :
1) 2018 ACJ 740, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India At New Delhi in between Manuswamy and others V/s.
Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Trans. Corpn. Ltd, wherein it is held as under:
"Quantum fatal accident Principle of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged :
21, contract worker in a company - High Court did not consider future prospects while computing compensation - Whether claimants are entitled to compensation after addition of 40 per cent of income of the deceased towards future prospects " -
Held : - yes.
2) 2018 ACJ 5, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, at New Delhi in between Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others wherein it is held as under :
"Quantum Fatal accident - Principles of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged 40

Held: Yes: there cannot be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork :
executing Court directed to respondent compute entitlement of claimants by adding 40 per cent of income for future prospect and make corresponding deduction towards personal expenses".

30. The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others), wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that: "In case permanent employee the addition should be 15% between the age of 50 and 60 years".

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand the deceased was aged 52 years at the time of accident and he was permanent employee.
Hence, towards future prospects 15% of the income has to be added.
So, 15% of Rs.74,678/ comes to Rs.11,201/-.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.85,879/- p.m.
(Rs.74678/- + Rs.11,201/-).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 11.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that if the number of dependents are 2 to 3, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

31. After deducting 1/3rd towards his personal expenses in Rs.85,879/- it comes to Rs.57,253/-
(85,879 - 28,626/-) and multiplier applied is 11 which comes to Rs.75,57,396/- (57,253X 12 X 11 =
Rs.75,57,396/-) which is rounding off Rs.75,57,400/-.
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.75,57,400/- towards loss of dependency.

In MFA No.1662/2023 (MV-D) between Chandrakala & another Vs Dilipkuamr & another,
decided on 2.07.2024, Hon'ble High court of Karnataka held that:
"Since the amount due under the head loss of future prospects is yet to become due, it would be illogical and illegal to direct the insurance company to pay interest on loss of future prospects. Therefore, out of the total compensation payable, the respondent No.1 is not liable to pay any interest on the compensation under the head loss of future prospects."

sentences.text: In view of the said dictum, the amount awarded under the head loss of future prospects does not carry any interest.

33. Hence, the future prospect of 40% out of loss of dependency has been calculated in order to exclude interest which would comes at Rs.11,33,610/- i.e., (Rs.75,57,400/-x 15/100 = 11,33,610/-).
34.

TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs. 1,32,000/-
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/-
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/-
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 16,500/-
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 10,000/-
of dead body 6. Loss of Dependency Rs.75,57,400/-
Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.77,82,400/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.
35. Regarding Liability : As already discussed in the Issue No.2, in this case the driver of the offending bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-A-9990(Udayaranga Bus) was charge-sheeted.
Further, there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle as on the date of accident.
Therefore, Respondent No.1 being the Owner and Respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is in the "Affirmative" and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".

Issue No.4

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.77,82,400/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.

(No interest on the compensation of Rs.11,33,610/-
awarded under the head of future prospectus)
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
However, Respondent No.2 being the insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount as stated supra with interest at the rate of 6% p.a within 60 days from the date of this award.

Compensation amount awarded to the Petitioners are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 50% to the Petitioner No.1 2) 25% each to the Petitioner No.2 and 3.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 by way of E- payment, after their proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 and 2 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of their choice.
Entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.3 shall be ordered to be paid to her by way of E-payment, after her proper identification.

The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
 Draw Award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.1,50,00,000/- for the death of Shivaswamy.T.E S/o Late Eshwaraiah in the Road Traffic Accident.
Due to the heavy impact, the Shivaswamy T.E fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Prior to the accident, said Shivaswamy T.E was hale and healthy and he was working as Technical Operator Drilling in the Central Ground Water Board and was earning a sum of Rs.79,978/- per month and he got one more promotion for Super-annuation.
The deceased family entirely depending on the income of the deceased.
The said accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-A-9990.
The Respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed its objection.
Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement to the main petition denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus.
Further it disputes issuance of policy of insurance in favour of the 1 st Respondent in respect of Udayaranga bus bearing Reg. No.KA-42-A-9990, the liability of this respondent company if any is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy and subject to valid and effective driving licence of the rider in question and subject to confirmation of 64VB of Insurance Act, 1938.
Further contended that the accident occurred on account negligence on part the deceased who was riding Motorcycle in rash and negligent manner and lost control and fell down.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the Petitioners prove that Shri.Shivaswamy.T.E S/o Eshwaraiah was died in the Road Traffic Accident which occurred on 02-01-2023 at about 10.30 a.m., on Mysore-Bangalore road, near Channapatna Police Training school, Ramanagara, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of bus bearing No.KA-42-A-9990?
2. Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Shri.Shivaswamy.T.E?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for? If yes,
what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
4. What Order or Award?
7. My answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative. Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 8.
Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioner that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-A-9990 and in the said accident, Shivaswamy.T.E had succumbed to the injuries.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore, contention of Respondent No.2 that the accident occurred on account negligence on part the deceased who was riding Motorcycle in rash and negligent manner and lost control and fell down does not have any water.
Therefore, his evidence would not be deciding factor for the negligence.
Only the fact of negligence is disputed by the respondent No.2.
Though the Respondent No.2 has taken contention that the accident did not cause due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, but it did not lead any evidence to substantiate its contentions.
The Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending bus has not chosen to contest the case.
Hence,
the petitioners successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of the offending bus.
Moreover, after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending bus and the driver of the bus had not challenged the charge sheet.
Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus bearing No.KA-42-A-9990 and due to the said accident,
Hence, it is held that the petitioners have proved that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Shivaswamy.T.E.
In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 52 years and his avocation is shown as Technical operator drilling in the Central ground water board and was earning a sum of Rs.79,978/-
per month.
The accident was occurred on 02.01.2023.
Hence, the age of the deceased Shivaswamy.T.E to be taken at 52 years for the purpose of Assessment of compensation.
18. In order to prove the income of deceased the petitioners have produced Last pay certificate of deceased marked at Ex.P.5.
Petitioner No.1 has to live remaining part of her life in the absence of her husband and the loss of a husband full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to a wife.
Petitioner No.2 has to live remaining part of his life in the absence of his father.
Petitioner No.3 has to live remaining part of her life in the absence of her son and the loss of a son full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to a son.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- each under the head of loss of consortium and Rupees 16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rupees 16,500/- towards funeral expenses.
opennyai_summary.arguments: 20. Learned counsel for the Respondent No.2 vehemently argues that travel allowance should be deducted from the gross salary for considering the income of deceased.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.75,57,400/- towards loss of dependency.
TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs. 1,32,000/-
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/-
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/-
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 16,500/-
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 10,000/-
of dead body 6. Loss of Dependency Rs.75,57,400/-
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is in the "Affirmative" and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
Sunitha.
: From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.77,82,400/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.77,82,400/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
(No interest on the compensation of Rs.11,33,610/-
awarded under the head of future prospectus)
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
However, Respondent No.2 being the insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount as stated supra with interest at the rate of 6% p.a within 60 days from the date of this award.
Compensation amount awarded to the Petitioners are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 50% to the Petitioner No.1 2) 25% each to the Petitioner No.2 and 3.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 by way of E- payment, after their proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 and 2 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of their choice.
Entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.3 shall be ordered to be paid to her by way of E-payment, after her proper identification.
